# Jubilees Chapter 20 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 20:2 — "love each his neighbor" vs. "love one another" vs. "love each other"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "love each his neighbor" | Literal of Ge'ez kuellu la-ḥabero |
| LOGOS | "love one another" | Standard English reciprocal |
| PNEUMA | "love each other" | Modern natural idiom |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Love one another" has appropriate formal register and echoes the biblical covenant formula. EMET's "each his neighbor" is awkward; PNEUMA's version is fine but less formal than the context demands.

---

## 20:4 — "rooted out" vs. "uprooted" vs. "destined to be uprooted"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "rooted-out from the land" | Hyphenated literal |
| LOGOS | "rooted out of the land" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "destined to be uprooted from this land entirely" | Explains the prophetic force |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Rooted out" is the established English rendering of this idiom. PNEUMA's "destined to be" adds interpretive weight not in the Ge'ez. EMET's hyphenation is unnecessary here.

---

## 20:5 — description of Sodom's sins

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fornication, and uncleanness, and the corruption among themselves" | Full literal list |
| LOGOS | "fornication, their impurity, and their mutual corruption" | Formal with slight compression |
| PNEUMA | "sexual depravity, their filth, and the corruption they had sunk into together" | Vivid dynamic rendering |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The three-element list is structurally significant in Jubilees' sin taxonomy; LOGOS preserves it cleanly. PNEUMA's "filth" for uncleanness is vivid but registers too low; EMET's triple "and" is acceptable but LOGOS restructures more elegantly.

---

## 20:8 — the divine name epithets

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "glorious and honored and great and splendid and wonderful and mighty" | Full six-epithet literal |
| LOGOS | "glorious and honored and great and splendid and wonderful and mighty" | Same as EMET |
| PNEUMA | "glorious, honored, great, magnificent, wonderful, and mighty" | Substitutes "magnificent" for "splendid" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS. The six epithets form a liturgical formula in Jubilees; both literal translators preserve it identically. PNEUMA's "magnificent" for "splendid" is minor but unnecessary deviation from the formula.

---

## 20:11 — destination of Ishmael and Keturah's sons

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the country of the east" | Literal qedmat |
| LOGOS | "the land of the east" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "the eastern lands" | Modern idiom |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Land of the east" is the conventional biblical phrase (cf. Gen 25:6); EMET's "country" is acceptable; PNEUMA's "eastern lands" (plural) doesn't reflect the Ge'ez singular.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
